corrections.was: son of Sally Leibholz and Friederike Schmul
corrections.now: NOT A BROTHER — the dates forbid it. Probably a cousin or nephew of the same family
corrections.source: Jacob was born at Schubin on 8 August 1884 and Georg at Hammerstein on 7 June 1884 — SIXTY-TWO DAYS APART. Two sons of one mother cannot be. Both dates are the Bundesarchiv's, independently of the family, and that arithmetic is what this correction rests on. *** THE WORDING BEFORE 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 ALSO SAID 'two hundred kilometres apart' AND CALLED GEORG 'a different Leibholz family'. BOTH ARE WITHDRAWN. *** SALLY LEIBHOLZ, JACOB'S OWN FATHER, WAS BORN AT HAMMERSTEIN ON 7 JULY 1847 and married at Szubin on 24 November 1874. The family had people in both towns, so the distance between them is not evidence of anything and the surname at Hammerstein is not a stranger's. What the dates rule out is BROTHERHOOD; what they leave standing is a cousin or a nephew in the town Sally came from. The Leibholz page has said exactly that in its 'A likelier reading' panel since the start — 'right surname, right family, wrong generation' — and this correction contradicted it. It no longer does.

THE TREE'S OWN DUPLICATE, not an outside record. The harvest holds this man twice: 9500005, born December 1923 at Johannesburg, with a death place and no date; and 9500160, listed as HIS SON, of exactly the same name, born circa 1923 at Pretoria, died 2 April 1963 at Sasolburg. A father cannot be born in the same year as his son, and the two die in the same small Free State town. They are one man, and the date of death is on the duplicate. *** INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OBTAINED, 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND IT DID NOT NEED THE ESTATE FILES. *** "South Africa, Civil Death Registration, 1953-1967" — Entry for JOHANNES ANTONIE OELOFSE DE WITT, 2 APRIL 1963, SASOLBURG, ORANGE FREE STATE, aged 40, born 1923 at PRETORIA (FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:DD9Y-PLT2). A national death register says what the tree's uncited duplicate said. IT ALSO SETTLES WHICH HALF OF THE DUPLICATE WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE BIRTHPLACE — Pretoria, not Johannesburg. AND IT RAISES A DOUBT ABOUT THE BIRTH DATE: the death register makes him 40 on 2 April 1963, and a second marriage found the same day — to ELSIE MARIE GEYER on 25 FEBRUARY 1950 (ark 1:1:6ZHR-NVYN) — makes him 27 then. The two ranges overlap at April 1922 to February 1923, and the tree's "December 1923" falls outside both. Declared ages are not proof; two of them thirteen years apart, agreeing against the same date, are worth recording. See data/dewitt-confirmed.tsv.

corrections.who: Johannes Antonie Oelofse De Witt (the younger)
corrections.was: son of Johannes Antonie Oelofse de Witt, born circa 1923 at Pretoria
corrections.now: NOT A SECOND PERSON — the same man as 9500005, duplicated
corrections.source: Same name, same birth year as his supposed father, same place of death, and a father-son relationship that is arithmetically impossible. The duplication also invented a wife for him — 'Unknown de Witt', 9500161, who exists only to be his mother — and gave Delina de Witt a half-brother who is really her father. Found by tools/audit-tree.py, 20 September 2026, which flags a parent under fourteen at a child's birth. *** DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED INTO 9500005. *** The DUPLICATES map in tools/build-register.py collapses records only where the pair shares AN IDENTICAL BIRTH AND DEATH DATE, and says in its own comment that those are not guesses. This pair does not meet that bar: the birth places differ, Johannesburg against Pretoria, one birth is 'circa' and only one record carries a death. It is a strong inference and not an identity, so both records stay in the register with this correction attached to them, which is what corrections are for. *** 20 SEPTEMBER 2026: THE BAR HAS BEEN PARTLY MET AND THE RECORDS STILL STAY APART. *** The civil death register gives the birthplace as PRETORIA, which is the duplicate's birthplace and not 9500005's Johannesburg, so the two records now differ on a point where an outside source backs one of them. That strengthens the inference that they are one man and does not turn it into an identity, because nothing yet ties the Johannesburg birth to anybody at all. Both records stay in the register.

corrections.was: a node in the family tree on the front page, flagged “Removed — she was nobody”
corrections.now: OFF THE TREE. Kept in the evidence layer and nowhere else
corrections.source: DAVID'S DIRECTION, 20 September 2026: “if this person is a nobody she really doesnt need to be in the tree. keep it in evidence but not on the main screen.” HE IS RIGHT AND THE PANEL WAS SELF-INDULGENT. Edwina Ann Wear was born EDWINA ANN GREEN and married BRUCE WALLACE WEAR — Leonard's younger brother — in 1980. She is a Wear by marriage and NO BLOOD RELATION TO DERRICK AT ALL. This archive had spent a day on her, decided she was a coincidence, and then left her standing in the tree across all three columns under a heading announcing that she had been removed. A withdrawal does not need a monument, and a family tree is for the family. WHAT SURVIVES AND WHERE: her burial at West Park on 8 July 2014 in the cemetery-register table on the Leonard page; the cancelled estate request 33157/2014 on the status page; the negative in data/negatives.json that uses her to bound the Johannesburg cemetery search; the reasoning on the DNA page; and Bruce's own 1980 marriage on his timeline, because that is a fact about Bruce. ONE THING CHANGED WITH HER. The PHYLLIS AGNES ROBERTSON node existed to explain Edwina's mother. It now points where it always should have — at GILLIAN AGNES LOUISA NEL, born Wear, born eleven months into that marriage and carrying Agnes in her own name.
